segments.title: Fairmile D Dog Boats and Britain's coastal fleet
segments.summary: The Fairmile D Dog Boat and Fairmile's rapid wartime production of coastal craft for the Royal Navy.
segments.body: The Fairmile D motor gun boat was known as the Dog Boat. Leonard C. Reynolds's book on the craft is recommended as a useful introduction to its history. Fairmile rapidly produced motor torpedo boats, motor gun boats, and motor launches that made up much of the Royal Navy's coastal fleet in World War II. The Fairmile B is the more familiar member of the family because so many launches and motor gun boats were based on it.

evidence.note: The transcript introduces the Fairmile D and describes Fairmile's output of coastal craft for the Royal Navy.

segments.title: Fairmile D weight and firepower compared with E-boats
segments.summary: At 109 tons, the Fairmile D was heavier than an E-boat and carried considerably more firepower.
segments.body: The Dog Boat was the large, powerful member of the Fairmile family. Its displacement was 109 tons, so it was heavier than an E-boat. It also carried considerably more firepower.

evidence.note: The transcript calls the D the big, powerful boat and gives its 109-ton displacement, E-boat comparison, and firepower.

segments.title: Fairmile D torpedo conversions and D-Day
segments.summary: Some Dog Boats traded part of their gun armament for torpedoes later in the war while retaining considerable firepower for coastal-force work around D-Day.
segments.body: Later in the war, the need for more motor torpedo boats led to guns being removed from some Fairmile Ds and torpedoes being fitted in their place. Both torpedo boats and motor gun boats were needed for coastal coverage around D-Day. Even after conversion, the Dog Boats retained a considerable gun battery because they still needed that firepower. The mixed armament added torpedo capability while preserving much of the D's strength as a motor gun boat.

evidence.note: The transcript describes replacing some guns with torpedoes while retaining firepower for D-Day coastal-force duties.

segments.title: A modern Fairmile D or Flower-class corvette?
segments.summary: The Fairmile D is suggested as an alternative model for a modern small warship when people call for a new Flower-class corvette.
segments.body: Calls for a modern Flower-class corvette prompt a question about the Fairmile D: why is the Dog Boat not proposed as a modern model? Its heavy gun armament provides the context for considering it alongside the corvette. The question remains open, with no modern specification or detailed comparison of the two designs developed here.

evidence.note: The transcript contrasts calls for a modern Flower-class corvette with the idea of a modern Fairmile D Dog Boat.
